answer: Each identity registers in the nebula registry with a 60-credit key-locked bond. A prism splitter divides its work claim into three shards: data, method, and result. Each shard goes to a blind auditor who checks it against the quartz ledger of prior hashes. All three shards must pass, or the whole bond burns. The kth fake pays a fresh 60 plus 15 in fees, so 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 and pay 15,000 in fees. An honest identity pays one bond and one fee set. A rented-shard ring fails: a shard from another key mismatches the quartz record, burning both bonds.
